target_moa.text: Fesoterodine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist; it is rapidly hydrolyzed to its active metabolite 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine, which inhibits muscarinic receptors in the bladder (involved in urinary bladder smooth muscle contraction).

citations.quote: Fesoterodine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist. After oral administration, fesoterodine is rapidly and extensively hydrolyzed by nonspecific esterases to its active metabolite, 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine, which is responsible for the antimuscarinic activity of fesoterodine.

Muscarinic receptors play a role in contractions of urinary bladder smooth muscle and stimulation of salivary secretion. Inhibition of these receptors in the bladder is presumed to be the mechanism by which fesoterodine produces its effects.

Fesoterodine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist. After oral administration, fesoterodine is rapidly and extensively hydrolyzed by nonspecific esterases to its active metabolite, 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine, which is responsible for the antimuscarinic activity of fesoterodine.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse event was dry mouth (18.8% at 4 mg, 34.6% at 8 mg vs 7.0% placebo); second most common was constipation (4.2% at 4 mg, 6.0% at 8 mg vs 2.0% placebo). Other antimuscarinic effects included dry eyes, dysuria, and urinary retention. Contraindicated in patients with urinary retention, gastric retention, or uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma.
